actions.justification: Mandatory first step — obtain detailed history including chief complaint, symptom onset, prior cardiac history, medications, and functional status to guide diagnosis and management.
Mandatory — perform focused physical exam including assessment for signs of heart failure (JVD, S3 gallop, crackles, edema) and hemodynamic status.
Mandatory — obtain 12-lead ECG to identify rhythm, conduction abnormalities, ischemia, or LVH that may indicate underlying etiology of heart failure or guide therapy.
Mandatory: BNP/NT-proBNP is essential for diagnosing and risk-stratifying heart failure, which appears to be the working diagnosis given the available action set.
Mandatory: Chest X-ray provides critical information on pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, and pleural effusions relevant to heart failure assessment.
Mandatory: BMP assesses renal function, electrolytes, and glucose — essential for guiding heart failure management and medication dosing.
Mandatory lab order - CBC to evaluate for anemia, infection, or other hematologic abnormalities contributing to cardiac symptoms.
Mandatory lab order - TSH to rule out thyroid dysfunction (hypo/hyperthyroidism) as a reversible cause of heart failure or cardiac symptoms.
Assess hemodynamic profile to classify volume and perfusion status, guiding further management decisions for this heart failure patient.

Echocardiographic assessment of LVEF is a critical next step in heart failure workup to guide therapy selection (beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, CRT, ICD). Not yet completed and essential for determining appropriate management pathway.
Once LVEF is known, ICD candidacy assessment is guideline-recommended for patients with reduced EF (typically <35%) to reduce sudden cardiac death risk in heart failure.

CRT indication assessment is guideline-directed for heart failure patients with reduced LVEF and evidence of dyssynchrony (LBBB, prolonged QRS on ECG already obtained), potentially improving outcomes.

NYHA functional classification is essential for guiding heart failure management decisions including medication titration, device therapy candidacy, and referral for advanced therapies. Has not yet been completed.
Assessment of structural abnormalities (e.g., valvular disease, chamber dilation) guides targeted therapy and identifies reversible causes of heart failure beyond what LVEF alone provides.
Evaluating candidacy for advanced heart failure therapies (LVAD, transplant) is appropriate once initial workup is complete, particularly if LVEF is reduced, to ensure timely referral if indicated.

With structural assessment, LVEF, NYHA class, and initial workup completed, evaluate whether patient is on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) duration and dosing for heart failure management.
Assess and address volume status/congestion as part of heart failure management after initial workup is complete.
Cardiac rehabilitation is indicated for eligible heart failure patients to improve functional capacity and quality of life per HF guidelines.
With workup largely complete, confirm that the patient is on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, reviewing current medications against guideline targets.
ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI is a cornerstone of HFrEF management per guidelines; with stable BP (120/80) and no contraindications identified, initiation or optimization is indicated.
Beta-blocker therapy is a Class I recommendation for HFrEF; patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80) making this an appropriate time to initiate or optimize beta-blocker dosing.

Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) is recommended in HFrEF patients already on ACE/ARB/ARNI and beta-blocker to reduce morbidity and mortality, provided renal function and potassium are acceptable (awaiting BMP results).

Patient has undergone extensive heart failure workup including GDMT optimization, ICD/CRT assessment, and candidacy for advanced therapies evaluation. Next step is comprehensive transplant workup to assess eligibility for cardiac transplantation as an advanced therapy option.
With advanced heart failure workup in progress, assess need for inotropic support to maintain perfusion and potentially as bridge therapy while advanced therapy options are evaluated.
